intro.zh-Hans: 不急着读完，先学会读懂一小段。
intro.en: Start small. Give one passage your full attention.

body.zh-Hans: 先读约翰福音第1章1—5节，再读到18节。记录谁在说话、出现了哪些重复词，以及哪些地方仍不明白。这里的“道”需要放在整段中理解；一句经文可以成为入口，却不能代替上下文。
body.en: Read John 1:1–5, then continue through verse 18. Notice the speaker, recurring words and questions you still have. The meaning of “the Word” develops across the passage. A single verse can be a doorway, but context matters.

question.zh-Hans: 遇到一句不懂的经文，先做什么？
question.en: What is a useful first step when a verse is unclear?

text.en: Read the surrounding passage and note your questions

feedback.zh-Hans: 这样可以保留作者的论述脉络。
feedback.en: This keeps the passage’s train of thought in view.

text.zh-Hans: 只看这句话，立即下结论
text.en: Draw an immediate conclusion from that sentence alone

feedback.zh-Hans: 先看上下文，再判断解释是否成立。
feedback.en: Check the surrounding passage before settling on an interpretation.

intro.zh-Hans: 让比喻帮助理解，不把比喻误当说明书。

body.zh-Hans: 诗篇23篇用牧者、道路、筵席等形象表达信靠。先读完整篇，再观察这些意象如何变化。文学体裁影响阅读方式：诗歌的画面与叙事中的事件记录并不相同。
body.en: Psalm 23 expresses trust through images of a shepherd, a path and a table. Read the whole psalm and notice how the imagery changes. Genre shapes interpretation: poetic images work differently from a narrative’s account of events.

question.zh-Hans: “耶和华是我的牧者”首先使用了什么表达？
question.en: What kind of expression opens Psalm 23?

feedback.zh-Hans: 用熟悉的形象表达照顾与引导。
feedback.en: A familiar image conveys care and guidance.

feedback.zh-Hans: 这里是诗歌，不是职业资料。
feedback.en: This is poetry, not an occupational record.

intro.zh-Hans: 留意行动，而不只给人物贴标签。
intro.en: Watch what people do, not just who they are.

body.zh-Hans: 读路加福音10章25—37节。耶稣用撒马利亚人的故事回应关于邻舍的问题。比较经过伤者身边的人做了什么，再读结尾的问答。导读的重点是文本中的行动，不是借故事贬低任何群体。
body.en: Read Luke 10:25–37. Jesus responds to a question about one’s neighbor with the story of a Samaritan. Compare the actions of those who encounter the injured man, then reread the closing exchange. Focus on the actions in the text rather than using the story to disparage a group.

question.zh-Hans: 故事结尾，怎样的人被认作邻舍？
question.en: Who is identified as a neighbor at the end?

text.en: The person who shows mercy through action

feedback.zh-Hans: 路加福音10章36—37节把重点放在怜悯上。
比较人物的行为，能看出这一差别。
feedback.en: Comparing their actions reveals the distinction.

intro.zh-Hans: 欣赏艺术，也分清画面与经文。
intro.en: Enjoy the painting while distinguishing image from text.

body.zh-Hans: 先读出埃及记2章，再欣赏《发现摩西》。画中的华丽服装属于画家对故事的重述。画作能帮助我们停留和观察，却不能被当作古埃及服装或建筑的直接证据。
body.en: Read Exodus 2 before looking at The Finding of Moses. Its elaborate costumes are part of the painter’s retelling. Art invites sustained attention, but the image is not direct evidence for clothing or architecture in ancient Egypt.

question.zh-Hans: 画中服装能直接证明圣经时代的穿着吗？
question.en: Do the painted costumes directly establish what people wore in biblical times?

text.zh-Hans: 不能，要区分故事时代与创作时代
text.en: No; distinguish the story’s period from the painter’s

feedback.zh-Hans: 经文与艺术史资料承担不同的证据作用。
feedback.en: Scripture and art-historical sources offer different kinds of evidence.

text.zh-Hans: 能，画面就是当时的记录
text.en: Yes; the painting is a contemporary record of the event

feedback.zh-Hans: 这幅画创作于16世纪，不是故事发生时的记录。
feedback.en: This is a sixteenth-century painting, not a contemporary record of the event.

intro.zh-Hans: 不以完成数量衡量每一次阅读。

body.zh-Hans: 读马太福音6章25—34节，注意关于忧虑的重复提问。试着用自己的话记录本段主题，再写下一个需要继续探索的问题。个人反思是阅读记录，不是新增经文，也不代替现实中的专业支持。
body.en: Read Matthew 6:25–34 and notice its repeated questions about worry. Summarize the passage in your own words, then carry one question into your next reading. Personal reflection is a reading response, not additional scripture or a substitute for professional support.

question.zh-Hans: 自己的阅读心得应怎样标注？
question.en: How should you describe your own reflection?

text.en: As a personal reflection, distinct from scripture

feedback.zh-Hans: 保留经文的出处，也给个人思考留下空间。
feedback.en: Keep the source clear while making room for your own thought.

feedback.zh-Hans: 个人表达与正式经文需要清楚区分。
feedback.en: Personal writing and the biblical text should remain clearly distinguished.
